acceptance_test_interpretation: The first test binds a closed, non-RNG finite preparation artifact and checks reproducibility, but cannot by itself establish semantic truth. The second exhaustively exercises the finite phase machine, public boundary, support/provenance, carriers, interventions, uncertainty, adverse terminals, and root reduction. The third checks paired-prefix equality and post-action taint closure against private-field and capability mutations. The fourth checks chronological, independently grounded, root-deduplicated provenance and transform specificity. The fifth fixes the scientific unit at registered environment roots and rejects omission, duplication, replay, or replacement. The sixth limits V7 reuse to explicitly mapped byte-identical primitives and checks that V7 authority and oracle material cannot reach PCFL actor state. The seventh freezes the model-free handoff surface so later M-TEXT cannot choose outcome-changing M0 semantics after implementation. The eighth measures the later narrow supplied-connected-text causal-use claim under a fixed model, goals, experiment choice, reset, controls, and noncompensatory endpoints. The ninth tests whether any positive result survives no-memory, raw-context, RAG, native-graph, organized-memory, masking, and twin controls. The tenth checks independent implementation review and separate scientific advocacy against exact M0 bytes before model-facing use; it is a governance gate, not a scientific result.

ambiguities.impact: If a separately ratified renderer/tokenizer/cut boundary can still choose output-affecting bytes after M0, the handoff is not actually frozen and later model results may reflect a redesigned instrument.
ambiguities.question: Must every renderer, tokenizer, parser, prompt projection, and cut identity be hash-bound before M0 handoff acceptance, or may a separately approved preparation packet bind them only before M-TEXT execution?

ambiguities.impact: The proposal requires a complete finite universe and canonical rows but does not itself enumerate the final deck, root identities, transition table, or all expected-reject bytes; these determine runtime state and test scale.
ambiguities.question: Is the candidate 64-root finite universe retained exactly, or will the later ratified manifest choose another universe and root count?

ambiguities.impact: Support status, contradiction precedence, revocation timing, alias normalization, and root identity affect which links become readable and therefore change carrier bytes and later model-visible evidence.
ambiguities.question: Where are the exact relation-specific support and revocation transition tables, including failure precedence, bound?

ambiguities.impact: The later loop has a frozen resource budget but no numeric call, read, context, generated-token, wall-time, or retry envelope here; different envelopes change the causal-use assay.
ambiguities.question: Which exact model-call, reader, context, output, and stop budgets are part of the separate M-TEXT ratification?

ambiguities.impact: Two checkers can reproduce the same erroneous manifest if they share the same derivation assumptions or source constants, so the meaning of independent reproduction is operationally important.
ambiguities.question: What distinct implementation, oracle, or invariant basis makes the second checker independent of the materializer and first checker?

assumptions: Human ratification will bind exact M0 bytes, the finite universe, reuse mapping, handoff fields, and scope; the current proposal state does not authorize preparation, implementation, or execution.

M0 public evidence means ordinary events and admitted provenance objects only. Private world state, hidden schedules, scores, branch traces, and receipts are not evidence available to an actor or later dream.

A thinker attempt can become future dream input only after it produces an eligible ordinary public outcome and passes the later package's chronological support boundary; a private working trace or failed branch cannot do so.
The M0 carrier is supplied-memory infrastructure and is not attributed to DREAM authorship. Future DREAM proposals, SLEEP consolidation, and LoRA state are separate packages.
LoRA, when eventually introduced, is parametric personal state transported transactionally from validated semantics; it is not an M0 or M-TEXT writer, discoverer, or working-memory store.
Registered environment roots are engineering/test units for M0 and do not become scientific sample size; goals, paths, calls, branches, cells, aliases, and reruns remain nested repeated measures.
claim_delta_interpretation: The graph separates three claim levels. M0 can establish only deterministic software conformity of a finite instrument, including its public visibility, provenance, intervention, and reducer contracts. Later M-TEXT can test only whether one fixed model uses supplied grounded connected text for changed-goal traversal, informative experiment selection, and delayed old-plus-new use. It cannot establish that DREAM authored the links, that an agent learned from its own life, that LoRA consolidated them, or that lifetime performance improved. Any failed M0 gate blocks model interpretation; any failed M-TEXT headroom, causal-use, or bypass control withdraws the corresponding supplied-memory claim and prevents that relay from being used as a LoRA premise. Parenting, accumulation, compression, baseline saturation, online feedback, and complete-organism behavior remain untested claims.

disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Bind a checker whose derivation is independently authored and whose critical invariants or reference values are not generated from the same materializer path; otherwise characterize the receipt as reproducibility only.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: The proposal treats two independently derived checkers reproducing one manifest root as falsifying a self-consistent single materializer. Agreement proves duplicate-free deterministic reproduction, but shared specification errors can survive it and semantic correctness is not established by agreement alone.
disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The independence acceptance criterion is stronger in wording than the operational evidence currently specified.

disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Require the separate preparation boundary to bind every output-affecting renderer, tokenizer, parser, prompt, and cut byte before any M-TEXT execution, and require the M0 handoff receipt to identify that immutable binding rather than an open-ended future choice.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: The graph says M0 freezes a read-only handoff, while the acceptance wording permits renderer/tokenizer/cut inputs or a separately ratified preparation boundary. If the boundary is resolved after M0 implementation, later choices can change actor-visible semantics and invalidate the claimed interface freeze.
disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The proposed alternative between frozen inputs and a separately ratified preparation boundary is not yet operationally equivalent.

disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Require an explicit human-bound PCFL scope extension or successor authorization that names each reused V7 primitive and confirms that prior V7 forbidden successor/model scope remains excluded; absent that artifact, treat V7 as design reference only.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: A new PCFL graph edge cannot by itself override the prior V7 ratification's terminal and successor restrictions or its failed external scope audit. Byte identity authenticates source bytes, not permission to use them in a new authority context.
disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The proposal correctly identifies a new reuse edge, but its phrase 'under new authority' must be interpreted as an explicit scope authorization, not merely a PCFL mapping record.

graph_delta_interpretation: The external V7 node supplies only named, byte-identified primitive mathematics to M0 checker/conformance code through a new PCFL-specific edge; no V7 authority, golden, oracle, expectation, terminal permission, or scientific meaning moves downstream. M0 is a new thin node containing the PCFL-specific finite deck/world, public event/view/command boundary, phase and reset state, finite reader, chronological support/provenance, connected carrier and interventions, uncertainty, and root receipts. M0 feeds model-free CPU conformance and a read-only handoff. Later M-TEXT consumes only the permitted public projection and supplied connected text plus ordinary public outcomes; its outputs remain root-local traces and cannot mutate M0 or upstream bytes. E0 and G are separate prerequisites, and only their conjunction with M-TEXT can later open an M-LORA package. No graph edge makes M0 a learned child, makes M-TEXT a DREAM author, or transfers credit to LoRA. Operationally, information moves from frozen internal world/deck state to public events and views, then through explicitly allowed public evidence and carrier projections; private world bits, intervention labels, branch workspaces, scores, and receipts terminate at checker/reducer boundaries.

open_questions: Rohin Ghosh must ratify the exact proposal bytes, finite universe, V7 primitive mapping and scope extension, deterministic materializer/checker boundary, M0-to-M-TEXT handoff, allowed files/tests, and prohibitions before any implementation or materialization.
The human decision must preserve that M0 is software evidence only and that M-TEXT, E0, G, M-LORA, L, P, C, O, and confirmation require separate approvals and gates.
No CPU preparation or test, model/tokenizer/provider call, writer or LoRA operation, GPU use, root selection, scientific estimator, or claim may be inferred from this interpretation.

loop_delta_interpretation: The first loop is a post-ratification deterministic preparation loop: it reads the ratified finite specification and named V7 hashes, writes a closed manifest/checker receipt/root, and stops at complete agreement; any mismatch, missing byte, forbidden dependency, or selection behavior fails closed. It has no RNG, search, ranking, favorable-root choice, retry, replacement, or model feedback. The M0 episode then reads frozen root/deck state, current public view, legal commands, registered carrier/intervention state, and chronological provenance. It emits ordinary public events, finite views, support/revocation state, and one final root receipt. Its phase schedule includes old discovery, dream/reference rendering, validation, isolated goal probes, a public join, uncertainty, acquisition, new validation/rendering, reset, delayed goal, and finalization. Probe branches have bounded action slots; views expose bounded read/action budgets; identical command retries yield two identical semantic returns and a third blocked return, while failed actions do not advance state; resets discard branch-local workspace, query cache, repeat state, and hidden branch history, and no retry or replacement creates another unit. Later M-TEXT is a goal-conditioned use loop: the fixed model retrieves supplied connected text through the common reader, chooses legal reads/actions, observes public outcomes, revises temporary working state, and writes only traces, public command/outcome records, and a root receipt. It does not author links, update parameters, train, or replace roots. In the deferred full organism, DREAM may propose broad target-independent local connections or re-expressions from eligible public experience, but only later independent public grounding can support them; SLEEP can then transactionally consolidate validated personal semantics into LoRA state; THINK retrieves and composes goal-relevant state, acts, observes, and revises. A thinker attempt or outcome becomes eligible evidence for a later dream only after the ordinary outcome is public, crosses the relevant phase/eligibility boundary, and satisfies chronological independent support. Private reasoning, abandoned branch state, dependency traces, correctness, scores, failure reasons, timing, and final receipts are discarded at joins or excluded from the later dream. None of this deferred Dream–LoRA–Think loop is instantiated by M0 or the supplied-text assay.
system_thesis_interpretation: The proposal preserves Dream–LoRA–Think as a complete organism while isolating its first measurable relay. In the deferred organism, action–outcome experience is first observed as grounded public transitions; DREAM manages breadth-like connection growth by proposing many target-independent local adjacencies or re-expressions, not by following a goal; later public support validates or revokes those proposals; SLEEP consolidates only validated personal semantics into transactional parametric LoRA state. THINK is different: it receives a goal, retrieves explicit declarative memory, constructs a goal-directed path through current state, acts, observes ordinary outcomes, and revises temporary working state. M0 contains explicit finite declarative nodes, links, transition rows, uncertainty records, public events, and receipts. It contains neither LoRA-parametric state nor a learned child. M-TEXT receives supplied declarative connected text and uses temporary model context/working traces, but writes no persistent parameters. Module-level credit is limited to structural receipts for the reader, support/provenance, carrier, intervention, and reducer; whole-organism credit is explicitly unavailable until separate packages establish causal behavior across organs. The first model assay therefore credits only supplied-memory use under a fixed model and registered roots, not discovery, consolidation, learning, lifetime improvement, or the online action–evidence flywheel. Scale is intentionally finite at M0; root identity fixes the unit, while internal paths, branches, goals, cells, aliases, calls, and reruns are repeated measures. Later scientific scale, sample size, slope, margin, and stopping rules are not inherited from the finite fixture.
visibility_matrix_interpretation: Visibility is stage-specific and directional. Authorization may inspect the manifest, private-world scope, public evidence, carrier contract, goals, intervention semantics, V7 mapping, receipts, and future prompt/interface bindings; this does not make them actor inputs. M0 reads the frozen manifest and private world only for internal transition/checking, emits canonical public evidence and supplied-carrier projections, and exposes no model/provider/tokenizer path. The actor sees only the legal finite view: phase/state, released goal, sorted legal actions, last public event, permitted uncertainty, returned memory objects and public IDs, explicit budgets, and registered repeat/reset status. It cannot see root bits, future goals, arm labels, intervention or oracle values, scores, goldens, schedules, filenames, errors, private handles, branch workspaces, retrieval transcripts, dependency traces, or receipt scores. Public IDs returned by the reader may later serve as anchors; unreturned catalog identities cannot. Padding, fixed slot counts, catalogs, reader order, and command bytes are exposure controls, not semantic evidence. Branch-local state is visible to M0 only as internal state and is explicitly excluded at fork/join/reset; GOALS_COMPLETE and ordinary public outcomes are the narrow join projection that can enter later acquisition/evidence flow. The checker sees private state, intervention labels, receipts, and V7 mappings to validate invariants, but none of those are forwarded to the actor or M-TEXT. M-TEXT receives only the frozen permitted public projection, supplied connected text, registered goal/prompt fields, and ordinary public outcomes; later model outputs remain local assay traces. Organism-private child, parent, writer, LoRA, lineage, and personal state are forbidden throughout this change.
